Ruben (vendor ops): DataStream SpA (CL) asked us to gross-up their invoice for 15% Chilean withholding. They attached a Certificado de Residencia (RUT 76.123.456-7).
Eleni (finance): Do we have a contractual gross-up clause? I don't see one in the PO. Normally vendor handles local withholding.
Sofia (tax): Certificate looks like a valid SII residency doc. Key question: which Redwood entity is making the payment (US, NL, or CL)? If payment originates from NL, Chilean WHT might apply.
Ruben (vendor ops): Vendor says payment will come from our NL billing entity. They insist we must gross-up to deliver agreed net.
Mila (payments): Policy: DO NOT GROSS-UP without legal/tax sign-off. I'll place a payment hold: "WHT/GROSS-UP DISPUTE".
Sofia (tax): Options for vendor: 1) Reissue invoice grossed-up (we pay total) + signed acceptance, or 2) We pay net and withhold per Chile rules, issuing a withholding certificate for their SII credit. We need payment routing proof.
Eleni (finance): Ask vendor to reissue or confirm they will accept a withholding certificate. Also send bank/payment instruction showing payer entity.
TaxBot: Reminder: save all docs to tax_evidence/2024/cl_datastream_76-123456-7 for audit.
Ruben (vendor ops): Sent vendor the two options and asked for payment routing proof. Holding payment until we get their choice or legal sign-off.
Sofia (tax): I'll review the Certificado and the contract. If vendor insists on gross-up, we'll require legal amendment and treasury approval. Will update EOD.
